en: The Hymn for Protection from Misfortune (Ārtatrāṇastotra)
Beholding the gods, beginning with Brahmā, being scorched by the poison produced from the churning of the ocean of milk, he who— out of compassion—
fearlessly swallowed the poison known as Hālāhala through his own playful power, protected the worlds with devotion.
Devoted to protecting those in distress, that Blessed One, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, is my refuge. || 1 ||
Having drunk sweet milk at his maternal uncle's house and then gone to his own home, he performed severe penance with a distressed mind due to the lack of milk;
out of compassion, [the Lord] granted Upamanyu an inexhaustible ocean of milk.
Devoted to protecting those in distress, that Blessed One, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, is my refuge. || 2 ||
He who, emerging from the Liṅga out of compassion, protected the sage Mārkaṇḍeya— who was solely devoted to meditating on his own feet— by striking Death upon the chest;
and who gave the desired discus to Hari by offering his lotus-eye.
Devoted to the protection of those in distress, that Blessed One, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, is my refuge. || 3 ||

Seeing the great Kaurava army led by Droṇa, Jayadratha, and other chariot-warriors, the Destroyer of the Affliction of Those Seeking Refuge protected Pārtha— who, though accompanied by Kṛṣṇa, was terrified—
proclaiming his divine weapon whose aim is never in vain.
Devoted to protecting those in distress, that Blessed One, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, is my refuge. || 4 ||
Seeing a young boy born of the Śiva lineage— who was surrounded by his own kinsmen and relatives,
who was distressed as he attempted to place a handful of flowers upon your head with hands raised in effort— Brahmā bowed down and performed worship to you in the beautiful city of Amarāvatī.
Devoted to protecting those in distress, that Blessed One, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, is my refuge. || 5 ||

In the past, when the hosts of gods and asuras were terrified by fear, he— Indra and the other eminent deities being rendered non-eminent— mounted upon his horse and, making the earth his chariot and the Vedas his steeds, took Murāri as his arrow;
out of compassion, he protected all the wise gods and in an instant conquered the enemies of the city (the Asuras).
The Blessed One, Gaṅgādhara, who is devoted to protecting those in distress, is my refuge.

In the past, he who was renowned as an ocean of compassion protected [his son] even once, though that son had turned his back on the path of Śruti and Smṛti, was rising toward great sins, and spoke thus: "My offspring alone, though transcending the universe, is my refuge."
Devoted to the protection of those in distress, that Blessed One, the bearer of the Gaṅgā, is my refuge. || 7 ||
In the past, when the venerable gods requested him to endure the force of the Gaṅgā,
Rudra, seeing the devoted Bhagīratha bowing before him,
compassionately released the purifying celestial river from the mass of his matted locks onto the surface of the earth.
The Blessed One, Gaṅgādhara, who is solely devoted to protecting those in distress—he is my refuge. || 8 ||
Thus ends the *Gaṅgādharastotra*, also known as the *Ārtatrāṇastotra*, composed by the illustrious Appayadīkṣita.
